title: Phish Gets Ready for Its 100th Show at Madison Square Garden
summary:
The rock band Phish is about to reach a big milestone. On January 2, the band will play its 100th concert at Madison Square Garden, the famous arena in New York City. That show will wrap up a four-night run of concerts there around New Year's Eve.

Phish first played at the Garden on December 30, 1994. Over the past 32 years, the band has returned again and again for single shows and longer runs called residencies. In 2017, Phish played 13 shows there in a run called the Baker's Dozen. A baker's dozen means 13, one more than a regular dozen. During those shows, the band played 237 songs without repeating a single one.

To celebrate reaching 100 shows, Phish put together a video featuring people who have worked at the arena during its concerts over the years. Ushers, bartenders, food sellers and merchandise sellers shared their thoughts. "I love the Phish," one worker says. Another says Phish fans are the only fans who ask how everybody is treating you. The video also shows the relaxed, swaying way Phish fans like to dance.

Tickets for the four New York shows go on sale to the general public at noon on October 16. Ticketmaster is already taking ticket requests.

Before the New York shows, Phish has concerts scheduled this month in Virginia, Florida and Alabama. After the New York run, the band will headline its own festival, Phish: Riviera Maya 2027, in Cancún, Mexico, in late January. The festival will include eight sets from the band, DJ sets from James Murphy and Questlove, and comedy from Fred Armisen and other comedians.
why_it_matters: Playing 100 shows at one arena shows how a band can build a loyal community over decades. The video also highlights the workers who help make concerts happen.

background_read: Madison Square Garden is a famous indoor arena in New York City that hosts concerts and sports games.
Phish is a rock band known for long live shows and for changing its song list from night to night, so many fans attend several concerts in a row.
When a performer plays a series of shows at one venue, it is called a residency.
Reaching 100 shows at one place is rare, because big arenas host many different performers.
